findings.title: Verified: clean rename, complete floor promotion, safe SQL, and tier-appropriate test coverage
findings.description: Description: Cross-checked against the working tree, not just the diff: (1) no import of the old `models.kalshi` path remains in `src/` or `test/`; (2) the `_effective_floor` → `effective_tape_floor` rename leaves no stale references and the docstring's "one spelling" claim holds — `read_trade_status` and `tape_facts` both call it; (3) every query in `serve_timeseries.py` composes via `psycopg.sql` with `%s`/`%(name)s` placeholders — identifiers come only from module-local constants (`kalshi.candlesticks`, `kalshi.trades`) with documented `noqa: S608` justifications, and `tape_filtered` evaluates the exact `trades_filter_sql` parameters rather than re-spelling the membership test, including the `COALESCE(s.category, '')` null semantics; (4) the `kalshi_dense_db` load fixture writes only into the `ephemeral_db` minted by the tier, with every column it inserts present in the kalshi track migrations; (5) the count-before-fetch guard has no `LIMIT`, matching the module's documented refusal-to-truncate contract, and the acknowledged count/fetch race (one row over the ceiling) is explicitly bounded and documented in the module docstring.

findings.title: Ceiling-sized response serialization runs on the event loop; the 34.80 MB candle case is the API's worst case
findings.description: Description: Both new handlers call `timeseries_response(response, fmt)` inside the `async def` after the executor returns. `model_dump(mode="json")` + `orjson.dumps`/`msgpack.packb` on 75,000 rows is synchronous CPU work on the loop; at the admission ceiling the candle response is the largest in the API (34.80 MB measured 2026-09-13, recorded in `test/load/test_188_kalshi_api_nfr.py:CANDLES_CEILING_RESPONSE_MB`), so a request at the ceiling can block the loop for well over 1 ms during encoding, stalling `/health` and other in-flight requests. This is not a defect introduced here: the bars path has serialized through the same helper since slice 187 (11.58 MB at ceiling, measured and bounded at 15 s), and the slice explicitly defers the byte-ceiling question rather than defending it ("Recorded here rather than asserted… not a threshold this slice defends"). Flagging for visibility only — the accepted open question lives in the load test's constant docstring, and any future byte ceiling or off-loop encoding should land against both route families at once.

findings.title: The trades 422 path asserts no fetch but not connection release, unlike the candles twin
findings.description: Description: `test_the_connection_is_released_before_the_refusal` (the 185 D8a claim: the 422 is raised after the checkout is returned, `pool.open_now == 0`) is written for the candlesticks route only. The trades counterpart, `test_trades_over_ceiling_is_422_and_skips_the_fetch`, asserts the 422 and that `fetch_trades` never ran, but does not check `pool.open_now == 0`. The `_read` closures are structurally identical, so the risk that the trades variant regresses is low; a two-line extension of the trades test (or parametrizing the existing one over both paths, as `TestUnknownMarket` already does) would make the release-before-refusal claim symmetric across both new routes.
